criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: All four required items addressed in detail: primary mission, need (bleaching statistics, [1]-[3]), single-spacecraft justification, and operator/customers clearly identified. Well referenced with literature. Only minor point: rationale for one satellite could quantify revisit trade vs constellation, but Section 2.3 covers this.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)
One satellite is therefore used. This also simplifies communications, reduces cost

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed: launch site/vehicle with justified trade table and azimuth calculation, orbit elements (Table 4) with correct J2 sun-synchronous derivation, explicit no-manoeuvre statement, STK access table for ground station, data budget, 5-year duration and drag-sail EOL. Hand calculations verified correct (decay, azimuth, spacing, data volume). STK screenshots and files provided. Link budget admittedly missing.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
There are six passes each day, three in the evening and three in the morning
With a 4 m² sail the satellite re-enters about two years after the end of the mission

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusions are specific and quantitative, summarising orbit, coverage, communications and EOL results, and honestly identify four limitations with concrete next-phase actions. Well beyond generic.

evidence.quote: The design has four limitations. First, Vega C has not yet flown
a 4 m² drag sail removes the satellite in about two years, compared with about 32 years without it

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear logical structure with executive summary, numbered sections, consistently labelled figures/tables, and all in-text citations [1]-[15] matching the reference list. Writing is professional. Minor flaws: references [4] and [15] lack proper article titles/authors, and some figures (STK 3D views) are low-information content.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat
The Space Review, article 3887 on drag sails for de-orbiting satellites.

requirements.where: Images 1-5; Appendix A lists STK files in ZYZZsat_STK.zip

technical_issues.issue: Assumes S-band/X-band equipment can be added to the Mount Pleasant radio astronomy antenna; no link budget performed (acknowledged by student).
Vega C unflown at time of writing; fallback considered, but release altitude uncertainty propagates to orbit design (acknowledged).
References [4] and [15] incompletely specified (no article title/author).
Eclipse duration of ~34 min stated without shown calculation, though plausible for 600 km SSO.

overall: Excellent, comprehensive mission design report. All task requirements met with verified hand calculations, STK evidence and files, honest limitations, and professional presentation. Minor deductions for missing link budget, contingent launch vehicle, and two incomplete references.

feedback.summary: Excellent, comprehensive mission design report for ZYZZsat. All task requirements are met, with verified hand calculations, STK screenshots and files, honest discussion of limitations, and professional presentation. Minor deductions arise from the missing link budget, reliance on the unflown Vega C, and two incomplete references. A very strong submission overall.
next_steps: Perform a full link budget for the S-band/X-band link to Mount Pleasant (Section 2.4), showing margin, to substantiate the six-passes-per-day communications claim.

Strengthen the launch justification by quantifying how release-altitude uncertainty for Vega C propagates into your orbit design (Section 2.3), and state explicit fallback orbit elements for the backup vehicle.
Complete references [4] and [15] with full article titles and authors, and consider replacing low-information STK 3D views with annotated figures that highlight key design parameters.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your Introduction addresses all four requirements in detail: the 5 m GBR imaging mission, need supported by bleaching literature [1]-[3], clear single-spacecraft justification, and identified operator (AIMS) and customers. To reach the very top, quantify the revisit-time trade-off between one satellite and a small constellation, even briefly, rather than relying on Section 2.3 to cover it.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (9/10). Your mission design addresses every requirement: justified Vega C/Kourou launch with azimuth calculation, correct J2-derived sun-synchronous elements (Table 4), explicit no-manoeuvre statement, STK access analysis (Table 5), data budget, and drag-sail EOL. Hand calculations were verified correct and STK evidence is complete. The next level requires closing the acknowledged gap: a link budget supporting the Mount Pleasant communications assumption.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (9/10). Your conclusions are specific and quantitative, summarising orbit, coverage, communications and EOL outcomes, and honestly identify four limitations with concrete next-phase actions (e.g. Vega C flight status, drag-sail re-entry in ~2 years vs ~32 years). This is well beyond generic; little further improvement is needed at this level.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (8/10). Your report has a clear structure with executive summary, numbered sections, consistently labelled figures/tables, and in-text citations [1]-[15] matching the bibliography. Writing is professional. To reach the top of the band, complete references [4] and [15] with titles/authors, and replace or annotate the low-information STK 3D views so every figure carries design content.
